headline: Sees upcoming major sporting events — Rugby World Cups and Brisbane 2032 Olympics — as catalysts to skyrocket media rights deals over the next decade
reasoning: Morton argues Australia is entering its biggest sporting decade in history, with the Men's Rugby World Cup in 2027, Women's Rugby World Cup in 2029 and the Brisbane Olympics in 2032 all on the horizon. These major events increase participation, attract sponsors and encourage investment in sporting infrastructure. While Australia's domestic population and viewership doesn't match Europe or the US, Morton believes the country is well on its way and that these events will dramatically increase the size of future media rights deals.
quote: Australia, we're entering our biggest sporting decade in history. We've got a lot of major events coming up. We've got the Rugby World Cup, the Men's Rugby World Cup in 2027, the Women's Rugby World Cup 2029 and of course the Brisbane Olympics in 2032. And you know, these major sporting events, they increase participation, attract sponsors and encourage investment in sporting infrastructure. These major events are going to skyrocket the media rights deals we see in the near future.
episode_title: Live sport rights explode as broadcasters pay premium for NRL

headline: Ryan Morton flags Australia's live sport rights as a high-value content asset, with NRL's $5.3bn deal signalling strong broadcaster willingness to pay a premium
reasoning: The NRL recently announced a $5.3 billion, seven-year media rights deal with Nine Network, Foxtel and Sky New Zealand, generating approximately $760 million per year in broadcasting revenue. Morton notes that media rights are historically the largest revenue source for sporting leagues, demonstrating strong growth in NRL viewership. He argues that broadcasters and streaming services are willing to pay a premium for live sport as other media formats diminish. Australia is described as entering its biggest sporting decade, with major events including the Men's Rugby World Cup (2027), Women's Rugby World Cup (2029) and Brisbane Olympics (2032) expected to further skyrocket media rights deals. These events increase participation, attract sponsors and encourage investment in sporting infrastructure.
quote: We're seeing a very promising and encouraging deal with the NRL. They just recently announced a $5.3 billion media rights deal with key channels being Nine Network, Foxtel and Sky New Zealand. So it's a seven year deal. And then sporting history and media rights is generally the largest revenue source for Sporting League. So it shows the growth in NRL viewership and that these broadcasters and streaming services are willing to pay a premium for these.
episode_title: Live sport rights explode as broadcasters pay premium for NRL
